name: Art Tower Mito
funding: Mito City endowed the Mito Arts Foundation with ¥100M and made it manager. 2026 supporters include Suntory, NEC, Joyo Bank, Genden Fureai Ibaraki Foundation and petroleum retailer Yoshida Sekiyu.
watch: Yoshida Sekiyu sells petroleum products and runs ENEOS stations in Ibaraki. Searches found no censorship or protest at Art Tower Mito.
why_flagged: Mito City endowed the Mito Arts Foundation with ¥100M and made it manager. 2026 supporters include Suntory, NEC, Joyo Bank, Genden Fureai Ibaraki Foundation and petroleum retailer Yoshida Sekiyu.
records_note: The foundation posts business reports and accounts for 2012 to 2024, shows 22 supporters as undated logos, and lists no directors.

name: Hara Museum ARC
funding: Run by the Foundation Arc-en-Ciel, set up in 1977 by Toshio Hara. Corporate supporting members (November 2021) include MUFG Bank, Mori Building, Takasago Thermal Engineering and Ikaho Country Club.
watch: Much of its energy comes from solar power. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Hara Museum ARC names eight corporate supporters as of November 2021 but posts no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: 21_21 DESIGN SIGHT
funding: Run by the Issey Miyake Design Culture Foundation. October 2026 corporate partners: Mitsui Fudosan, Miyake Design Studio, Issey Miyake Inc and Shiseido as main partners, plus 20 other firms.
watch: Main partner Mitsui Fudosan co-develops Jingu Gaien; ICOMOS issued a Heritage Alert on 5 September 2023 and a petition drew about 225,000 signatures.
why_flagged: Main partner Mitsui Fudosan co-develops Jingu Gaien; ICOMOS issued a Heritage Alert on 5 September 2023 and a petition drew about 225,000 signatures.
records_note: The site names 4 main and 20 other corporate partners, undated, and the Miyake foundation lists officers, but no reports or accounts.

name: Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo
funding: Tokyo Metropolitan Government museum; budget about ¥1B.
watch: Bloomberg is a current funder (Students Day, Oct 2026). Also a censorship row in Jul 2015, when MOT and Tokyo asked for an Aida family work to be removed and then withdrew the request.
why_flagged: Bloomberg is a current funder (Students Day, Oct 2026). Also a censorship row in Jul 2015, when MOT and Tokyo asked for an Aida family work to be removed and then withdrew the request.
records_note: MOT posts annual reports for fiscal 2008 to 2025; its operator foundation posts financial statements for 2015 to 2025 and names directors. No sponsor list.

name: Nezu Museum
funding: Chairman Koichi Nezu is honorary chairman of Tobu Department Store; councillor Yoshizumi Nezu chairs Tobu Railway.
watch: The claim that it takes no Tobu Group donations is not on its site. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Nezu posts yearly reports from FY2012, settled accounts and a full list of directors and councillors, and names no donors or sponsors.

name: Watari-um
funding: Founded by Shizuko Watari in 1990 out of her Galerie Watari; the owner's residence is in the building.
watch: Self-funded family museum with no published budget. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The private museum's site lists membership tiers but no annual reports, accounts, donor names or board.

name: Towada Art Center
funding: Municipal museum run for Towada City by Nanjo and Associates Group. August 2026 corporate members include Towada Gas. City FY2018 records show ¥17.7M siting funds and a ¥5M grant.
watch: Towada Gas sells gas and kerosene and is a top-tier S course member. The claim that nuclear grants built the museum is not confirmed.
why_flagged: Municipal museum run for Towada City by Nanjo and Associates Group. August 2026 corporate members include Towada Gas. City FY2018 records show ¥17.7M siting funds and a ¥5M grant.
records_note: The centre lists its corporate members as of August 2026, but posts no annual reports or accounts and names no board.

name: Yokohama Museum of Art
funding: FY2024 income ¥1.10B: ¥881M city management fee through the Yokohama Arts Foundation, ¥91M own projects, ¥23M fees, ¥40M city support. Five HEART to ART corporate partners.
records_note: The museum posts reports and settled accounts for FY2020 to FY2024 and names corporate supporters, undated; its operator posts a dated board list.

name: Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute
funding: Non-profit founded 2020 by artist Michael Armitage; no funder list on its site as of Oct 2026, only unnamed library donors.
watch: Supporter roster unverified. No roster published: About/programme pages name no funders, /support is 404. Search turned up only programme partners (Triangle, KSB TURN2).
records_note: Its site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; partners appear only inside event descriptions.

name: Rencontres de Bamako
funding: Mali's Ministry of Culture organises and the Institut français co-produces. Royal Air Maroc is a long-time partner. No full funder list is published.
watch: African photography biennale since 1994. The 15th edition runs 26 November 2026 to 26 January 2027. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: The festival site names its 2026 partners, led by Mali's culture ministry, with earlier editions filterable, but posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Museo Experimental El Eco
watch: Entrepreneur Daniel Mont paid for the 1953 building by Mathias Goeritz. UNAM bought and reopened it in 2005. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: El Eco has no records of its own; owner UNAM posts audited annual accounts for 2022 to 2025 and names its governing boards.

name: Museo Universitario del Chopo
watch: Sol Henaro has directed it since 2024. A Juan Gabriel show due 28 May 2026 was postponed with no reason given.
records_note: The Chopo's site names no sponsors; owner UNAM posts audited accounts for 2022 to 2025 and names its governing boards.
